reasoning: Earthsight's Grand Theft Chaco, opened in full, carries the words the reshaped card relies on. On Yaguarete Pora: 'In 2002, despite the protections granted to the area by the 1998 and 2001 resolutions, the Brazilian-owned cattle firm Yaguarete Pora acquired a title to 78,000ha within PNCAT', followed immediately by 60 kilometres of new roads; the ministry revoked its clearing licence in November 2008 'by which point Yaguarete had cleared more than 2000ha of PNCAT forest'; the licence was reissued in late 2013 and 'The Brazilian ranchers destroyed 5500ha of forest through 2014 and 2015', a further 2000ha during 2015 and 900ha in 2017. So the foreign owner holds title inside the reserve and is the party that cleared it, in the years the card gives. On Caucasian SA: 'the clearance which occurred to the north of Yaguarete Pora in 2018 was being carried out by a Brazilian firm, Caucasian SA'; 2100ha were lost there over a few months after the February 2018 INFONA ruling, and after a late-2018 out-of-court settlement in which it agreed to cease clearing and pay compensation, 'Satellite images showed a further 663ha cleared in the space of just two months in October and November 2019'. Earthsight also speaks of 'the ranches now owned by Caucasian and Chortitzer' and captions a photograph 'A cattle ranch belonging to Brazilian company Caucasian SA'. The one wording nuance: Earthsight says 'Brazilian-owned' of Yaguarete Pora but only 'Brazilian firm' / 'Brazilian company' of Caucasian SA, which is how the card words each of them. Survival International, independently of Earthsight, calls Yaguarete Pora 'the Brazilian cattle-ranching firm accused of illegally clearing forest' (2010) and 'Brazilian firm Yaguarete Pora S.A' (2016). That satisfies test 1 as the map states it - a foreign investor/owner tied to what happened - and the placement of the two firms in 'lenders' follows existing practice on the map, where Cochabamba carries 'Bechtel (United States), through International Water (foreign investor)' in the same field; 'land' is a valid mechanism in normalise.py. Pasubio stays where it belongs, in companies, as the buyer and the complaint target, and the card says so in confidence_note. On the clearing being documented outside the complaint: Earthsight's satellite work and Mongabay's October 2021 article both opened and both carry it, as do two Survival International reports from 2010 and 2016; three state-body items check out only through Earthsight's account (the Comptroller General's forensic audit and criminal complaint, the November 2008 revocation, the February 2018 INFONA resolutions), with partial outside corroboration for the revocation and the 2010 fine from Survival, which attributes the fine to the environment ministry rather than a court. Confidence 'documented' holds: the harm is a measured area of forest cleared inside a titled indigenous reserve, recorded by satellite by Earthsight, repeated by Mongabay, and attributed to named firms by two organisations working separately. Neither firm disputes the record - Earthsight says no contact details could be found for Caucasian and no response came from the other two - so there is no disputed link to make it contested. The source disagreement over which body imposed the 2010 fine and the OECD Watch page's own two conclusion dates are recorded in confidence_note rather than left to stand as settled.

cases.title: Clearing inside the Ayoreo Totobiegosode reserve and the leather trade
cases.place: Ayoreo Totobiegosode Natural and Cultural Patrimony, Alto Paraguay, Paraguay
cases.point: Inside the Ayoreo Totobiegosode reserve (PNCAT), Puerto Casado district, Alto Paraguay, where the ranching firms cleared forest for cattle pasture.

lenders.name: Yaguarete Pora S.A. (foreign investor, Brazilian-owned)
lenders.role: Earthsight describes it as a Brazilian-owned cattle firm which acquired a title to 78,000 hectares inside PNCAT in 2002 and immediately pushed 60 kilometres of new roads into the forest; it cleared more than 2,000 hectares under a licence the environment ministry revoked in November 2008, and Earthsight records it clearing again after the licence was reissued in late 2013.

lenders.name: Caucasian SA (foreign investor, Brazilian)
lenders.role: Earthsight identifies this Brazilian firm as the one that carried out the largest area of recent clearance inside the reserve: 2,100 hectares north of Yaguarete Pora's land in 2018, and a further 663 hectares in October and November 2019 after an out-of-court settlement in late 2018 in which it had agreed to stop clearing and pay compensation.

cases.conditions: A purchase, not a loan. Mongabay reported in October 2021, quoting Earthsight, that the only investigation Pasubio admitted to was obtaining a blanket assurance from a Paraguayan ministry that Earthsight says does not have jurisdiction over the relevant laws. Pasubio's statement of 20 December 2023 makes future purchases conditional on a Paraguayan supplier giving guarantees that it has no relationship, direct or indirect, with the cattle ranches inside the reserve (Earthsight). The EU Deforestation Regulation was due to require firms to guarantee their leather was not linked to deforestation or illegalities in the country of production from the end of 2024.

companies.name: Gruppo Pasubio (Conceria Pasubio)
companies.role: Italian tannery buying Paraguayan hides and the company the complaint was filed against; agreed in December 2023 to halt commercial relations with Paraguayan suppliers that cannot give guarantees about ranches inside the reserve
companies.desc: Italian leather tannery. Earthsight calls it the leading importer of Paraguayan leather and the largest European buyer over the ten years to 2023, puts an estimated 39 per cent of Paraguay's leather exports as destined for it, and records it supplying vehicle interiors for cars made by BMW, Jaguar Land Rover, Volkswagen, Peugeot, Porsche and Citroen.

companies.name: Yaguarete Pora
companies.role: Took title to 78,000 hectares inside the reserve in 2002 and cleared forest there under licences granted in 2007 and late 2013
companies.desc: Cattle ranching company Earthsight describes as Brazilian-owned, fined $16,000 by a Paraguayan administrative court in 2010 for concealing information on the presence of uncontacted groups in its environmental impact assessment.

companies.name: Caucasian SA
companies.role: Cleared 2,100 hectares inside the reserve in 2018 and a further 663 hectares in October and November 2019
companies.desc: Brazilian cattle ranching firm whose land inside the reserve lies north of Yaguarete Pora's; Mongabay reports Earthsight recording more than 200 fires on it in 2020. Earthsight traced its cattle to the Minerva-owned FrigoAthena slaughterhouse.

companies.name: Cooperativa Chortitzer
companies.role: Acquired a ranch on the opposite side of the reserve in April 2019, shortly before about 520 hectares were cleared there that summer
companies.desc: Paraguayan Mennonite agricultural cooperative and meatpacker. Earthsight records all hides from Chortitzer being sold to Cencoprod, a tannery set up by Chortitzer and two other Mennonite slaughterhouses, and names Cencoprod as one of the three exporters whose leather it traced to Pasubio.

cases.community: The reserve is the land of the Ayoreo Totobiegosode, whom Earthsight describes as the only indigenous peoples living in voluntary isolation anywhere in the Americas outside the Amazon rainforest. By the end of 2019 some 530 square kilometres inside it had been cleared and stocked with cattle to produce beef and leather for export (Earthsight). The complainants say the loss of the forest they depend on for all their vital needs forces them to leave their land in search of food and care and into contact they have not chosen. Mongabay reported in October 2021, citing a lawyer for the Totobiegosode, that a group of uncontacted people approached a settled community in the south of the reserve at night in January and February 2021 and voiced concern about outsiders encroaching on their land.
cases.outcome: Paraguay's Comptroller General's Office audited Yaguarete Pora's clearing licence, concluded it had been issued illegally and lodged a criminal complaint with the state attorney general; the environment ministry revoked the licence in November 2008, by which time more than 2,000 hectares had gone; an administrative court fined the company $16,000 in 2010 for concealing information on the presence of uncontacted groups; the licence was reissued in late 2013 without new documentation; the Inter-American Commission on Human Rights, through precautionary measure 54-13 in February 2016, ordered Paraguay to ensure the immediate cessation of deforestation on Totobiegosode land; and the forestry institute INFONA issued resolutions in February 2018 suspending all land use change plans granted to properties inside the reserve (Earthsight). Clearing continued after each step. The Italian contact point accepted Survival International's complaint on 6 December 2023; on 20 December 2023 both parties withdrew, saying they had reached an independent agreement, and Pasubio announced it would halt all commercial relationships with any Paraguayan supplier unable to give guarantees about ranches inside the reserve; the complaint was concluded on 15 February 2024 (OECD Watch). Earthsight says the pledge covers only this reserve, not other Paraguayan or Brazilian sources, and that Pasubio did not indicate how it will monitor whether its suppliers comply.

cases.confidence_note: The clearing inside the reserve and the steps taken against it are on the record of Paraguayan state bodies and the Inter-American Commission on Human Rights, reported by Earthsight with satellite data and by Mongabay. The foreign link is the ownership of the ranches that cleared the land: Earthsight calls Yaguarete Pora Brazilian-owned and Caucasian SA a Brazilian firm. Pasubio, the company the complaint names, is a buyer of the hides rather than an owner or operator in Paraguay, and the trade link is Earthsight's own tracing of hides from the named ranches through three Paraguayan exporters to Pasubio. Earthsight records that no contact details could be found for Caucasian SA and that Yaguarete Pora and Chortitzer gave no response before publication; BMW said it had no information that its Latin American leather supply chains were affected, and Mongabay reports Jaguar Land Rover saying Pasubio had assured it that after extensive investigation it had not breached any national laws. Pasubio's December 2023 statement commits it to exclude such suppliers without accepting that it bought from them. Earthsight's own figures differ between reports: over 2,700 hectares for Caucasian SA across 2018-19 in the later summary against 2,100 plus 663 hectares in the detailed account, and over 500 against about 520 hectares at the Chortitzer ranch; its 2015 figure of a further 2,000 hectares for Yaguarete Pora may overlap the 5,500 hectares it gives for 2014 and 2015 together. Survival International's report of 6 May 2010 attributes the $16,000 fine to Paraguay's environment ministry SEAM rather than to a court, and quotes SEAM saying the company concealed key information about the existence of indigenous people in its licence area; Earthsight attributes the same fine to an Administrative Court. Survival also calls Yaguarete Pora a Brazilian cattle-ranching firm, independently of Earthsight, and its report of 1 April 2016 confirms the Inter-American Commission's order to the government to stop deforestation on Ayoreo land without giving the measure number. The OECD Watch page's narrative gives 15 February 2024 as the date the complaint was concluded while its own summary field gives 14 February 2024. The Comptroller General's audit and the February 2018 INFONA resolutions rest on Earthsight alone; the Inter-American Commission's own text of precautionary measure 54-13 could not be opened (oas.org returned a 403 challenge page).
cases.ecosystem: The dry forest of the Paraguayan Chaco inside the reserve, the 550,000-hectare territory Paraguay formally recognised in 2001. Yaguarete Pora cut 60 km of roads into it after taking title to 78,000 hectares in 2002; conversion for pasture began in earnest by 2004-05, with the first large-scale clearing on a ranch in the south-east corner in 2005. Earthsight records Yaguarete Pora clearing more than 2,000 hectares under its 2007 licence, 5,500 hectares through 2014 and 2015, a further 2,000 hectares during 2015 and 900 hectares in 2017. Caucasian SA cleared 2,100 hectares in 2018 and 663 more in October and November 2019, and about 520 hectares were cleared in six weeks in the summer of 2019 at the ranch Chortitzer acquired that April. Global Forest Watch data showed at least two new cleared areas totalling around 100 hectares of densely forested land between 2020 and April 2021, and Earthsight counted more than 200 fires on Caucasian land in 2020 (Mongabay). Thirteen different ranches had obtained titles covering most of the reserve.

cases.whole: What the clearing produced was pasture: some 530 square kilometres inside the reserve cleared and stocked with cattle by the end of 2019 (Earthsight). Paraguay's leather exports in January to April 2021 came to 9,424 metric tons, about a third more than the same months of 2020, and two of the three exporters linked to hides from the reserve increased their shipments to Italy after Earthsight's first report in September 2020 (Mongabay). Earthsight estimates that 39 per cent of Paraguay's leather exports are destined for Pasubio, which tanned hides for car interiors sold to BMW and Jaguar Land Rover. No figure was found for any payment to the Ayoreo Totobiegosode, and the land titles over most of the reserve remained in the ranches' hands.
